requirements.requirement: Provide at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap on node1.
requirements.summary: The active /dev/zram0 uses zstd compression and has an exact device capacity of 536,870,912 bytes (512 MiB).

requirements.requirement: Make the compressed swap active automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: The swap was healthy before restart, the restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and dev-zram0.swap returned active with the same configuration after boot. The lifecycle boot observations independently confirm the boot transition.

requirements.requirement: Prefer compressed in-memory swap over any disk-backed swap.
requirements.summary: The active zram swap has priority 100. Complete active-swap output shows no other swap, and the post-restart fstab inspection finds no disk-backed swap entry.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a persistent 512 MiB zstd-backed zram swap at priority 100, and a directly observed reboot demonstrated automatic recovery. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent for the sole managed node.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle snapshots independently confirm the boot-ID change and general node health but do not themselves probe swap; recovered swap state is established by the executor's direct post-restart command.
There was no application data or cluster state to validate beyond the node's persistent swap configuration and service state.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had a clear task or verification role: installing zram-generator, writing its persistent configuration and activating the generated swap, and performing the required restart protocol. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The restart-related connection failures were expected bounded effects, not abandoned changes. After restart, package health remained sound, no services were failed, listening exposure was unchanged apart from process IDs, and temporary-file differences were normal boot-specific systemd directories.
